notes: Ten Standard items were queued and five were read; four name no street number. The jeweller's shop story is a burglary at a named shop whose address the article never prints, and it is a story about a person's loss in any case. The one address hit is in the weekly events column and is declined below.

coverage.note: One numbered address across five stories, in the events roundup.

findings.description: Recorded so the listing is not read again. A one-evening night market listed in the Standard's weekly events column, with the address given as the venue and nothing said about the building itself.

citation.label: The San Francisco Standard, “The best events in SF this week, from Black Pride to dance and film festivals,” 26 August 2026

raw.text: Local musicians headline this end-of-summer night market.

publish.note: Declined on the ten-year test. An events listing names a venue; it says nothing about the building, and the roundup headline names none of its listings, so there is no usable entry even if the fact were one. The resolver has since put the address on parcel 3755079; the decline is about the story, not the address.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 1145 FOLSOM ST → parcel 3755079; sf-parcels has blklot 3755079 active, 1145–1147 FOLSOM; the 2025 roll records it as commercial hotel, built 1983. The assessor files the parcel as 10 HALLAM ST. EAS puts 1145, 1147 FOLSOM ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 1145.
resolution.note: No page at this path yet; the parcel is the publisher's to seed.
